'''Drew Eubanks''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|j|uː|b|æ|ŋ|k|s}} {{respell|YOO|banks}};<ref>{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}}</ref> born February 1, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State Beavers]].

==Early life==
Eubanks was born in [[Starkville, Mississippi|Starkville]], Mississippi, and lived in [[Louisville, Mississippi|Louisville]], Mississippi, before moving to [[Troutdale, Oregon|Troutdale]], Oregon, at age 2.<ref>{{cite web |title=#12-Drew Eubanks |url=https://osubeavers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3189 |publisher=OSUBeavers.com}}</ref>

==College career==
Eubanks played for the [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State Beavers]] of the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]]. He was rated a 4-star recruit who was rated No. 1 in the state of Oregon and committed to the Beavers over Cal, Gonzaga, Oregon, and others.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Drew-Eubanks-76023|title=Drew Eubanks, Oregon State Beavers, Power Forward|website=247Sports|access-date=April 2, 2018}}</ref>

Eubanks averaged 14.5 points, 8.3 rebounds and 2.2 blocks per game as a sophomore on a team that won five games. As a junior, Eubanks averaged 13.2 points, 6.8 rebounds and 1.7 blocks per game. He declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] after the season, forgoing his final season of collegiate eligibility.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Moran|first1=Danny|title=Drew Eubanks declares for NBA draft and hires agent; will forgo senior season|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/index.ssf/2018/03/drew_eubanks_declares_for_nba.html|access-date=April 2, 2018|work=OregonLive|date=March 30, 2018}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===San Antonio Spurs (2018–2022)===
After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Eubanks signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for NBA Summer League play.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Daschel|first1=Nick|title=NBA draft: Oregon State forward Drew Eubanks is undrafted, will play summer league with San Antonio Spurs|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/index.ssf/2018/06/nba_draft_2018_oregon_state_be.html|access-date=June 23, 2018|work=OregonLive|date=June 22, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2018-utah-summer-league-roster|title=SPURS ANNOUNCE 2018 UTAH SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|date=June 28, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 28, 2018}}</ref> On September 17, 2018, Eubanks signed a two-way deal with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Spurs Sign Drew Eubanks To Two-Way Deal|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/251145/Spurs-Sign-Drew-Eubanks-To-Two-Way-Deal|access-date=October 16, 2018|work=realGM.com|date=September 17, 2018}}</ref> Eubanks made his NBA debut on October 20, 2018, in a 108–121 loss against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], playing three and a half minutes and scoring two points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.expressnews.com/spurs-nation/article/Notebook-After-brawl-Spurs-will-see-13325270.php|title=Notebook: After brawl, Spurs will see short-handed version of LeBron's Lakers|first=Jeff|last=McDonald|work=[[San Antonio Express-News]]|date=October 21, 2018|access-date=December 5, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201810200POR.html|title=San Antonio Spurs at Portland Trail Blazers Box Score, October 20, 2018|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 5, 2018}}</ref>

On November 24, 2020, Eubanks re-signed with the Spurs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-re-sign-drew-eubanks|title=Spurs re-sign Drew Eubanks|date=November 24, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 24, 2020}}</ref>

On 10 February 2022, Eubanks, [[Thaddeus Young]], and a 2022 second-round selection were traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[Goran Dragić]] and a 2022 first-round draft selection.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-acquire-goran-dragic-2022-first-round-pick|title=SPURS ACQUIRE GORAN DRAGIĆ & 2022 FIRST ROUND PICK|work=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2022}}</ref> He was subsequently waived.

===Portland Trail Blazers (2022–2023)===
On February 22, 2022, Eubanks signed a 10-day contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN DREW EUBANKS AND BRANDON WILLIAMS|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-drew-eubanks-and-brandon-williams|website=NBA.com|date=February 22, 2022|access-date=February 22, 2022}}</ref> He signed a second 10-day contract on March 4,<ref>{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN DREW EUBANKS TO SECOND 10-DAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-drew-eubanks-second-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 4, 2022|access-date=March 17, 2022}}</ref> a third 10-day contract on March 14<ref>{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN KRIS DUNN & DREW EUBANKS TO 10-DAY CONTRACTS|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2022/3/14/trail-blazers-sign-kris-dunn-drew-eubanks-to-10-day-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=March 14, 2022|access-date=March 17, 2022}}</ref> and a fourth on March 24.<ref>{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN KRIS DUNN & DREW EUBANKS TO 10-DAY CONTRACTS|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2022/3/24/blazers-sign-kris-dunn-drew-eubanks-to-10-day-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=March 24, 2022|access-date=March 24, 2022}}</ref> On April 3, he signed a contract for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN KRIS DUNN & DREW EUBANKS FOR THE REMAINDER OF THE SEASON|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2022/4/3/blazers-sign-kris-dunn-drew-eubanks-for-season|website=NBA.com|date=April 3, 2022|access-date=April 3, 2022}}</ref>

On July 7, 2022, the Trail Blazers re-signed Eubanks to a 1-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|author=Cowley|first=Jared|date=July 1, 2022|title=Drew Eubanks agrees to re-sign with Trail Blazers on 1-year deal: Report|url=https://www.kgw.com/article/sports/nba/blazers/drew-eubanks-portland-trail-blazers-one-year-deal/283-b38137b3-ca46-47e1-b487-9ddba9c9663a|access-date=July 4, 2022|work=[[KGW]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Re-Sign Drew Eubanks|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-re-sign-drew-eubanks|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2022}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2023–2024)===
On July 4, 2023, Eubanks signed a 2-year, $5 million deal with the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|title=SUNS SIGN KEITA BATES-DIOP, DREW EUBANKS, CHIMEZIE METU AND YUTA WATANABE|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-keita-bates-diop-drew-eubanks-chimezie-metu-and-yuta-watanabe|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 4, 2023|date=July 4, 2023}}</ref> After making his debut with the Suns on October 24,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/game/phx-vs-gsw-0022300062/box-score|title=Phoenix Suns vs Golden State Warriors Oct 24, 2023 Box Scores|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> the NBA announced on October 25 that the Suns lost one of the second-round picks they had the rights to at the time for the [[2024 NBA draft]] due to being in contact with Eubanks before the 2023 free agency period began.<ref>{{cite web | last=Conway | first=Tyler | title=Phoenix Suns Lose 2nd-Round Pick for Drew Eubanks Tampering Ahead of Free Agency | website=Bleacher Report | date=2023-10-25 | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10094782-phoenix-suns-lose-2nd-round-pick-for-drew-eubanks-tampering-ahead-of-free-agency | access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref> On [[Valentine's Day|February 14, 2024]], Eubanks was punched in the face by [[Detroit Pistons]] F/C [[Isaiah Stewart]] hours before the Suns' home game against the Pistons at the [[Footprint Center]] began. Despite the punch, Eubanks would still play for the Suns that night, putting up 6 points and 6 rebounds in 18 minutes for Phoenix's 116–100 win over the Pistons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202402140PHO.html|title=Pistons vs Suns, February 14, 2024|website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> On June 21, 2024, Eubanks declined his $2.6 player option with the Suns entering free agency.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Duenas |first=Brandon |date=2024-06-21 |title=Drew Eubanks declines $2.6M player option, set to become unrestricted free agent |url=https://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2024/6/21/24183361/drew-eubanks-declines-2-6m-player-option-set-to-become-unrestricted-free-agent |access-date=2024-06-24 |website=Bright Side Of The Sun |language=en}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2024–2025)===
On August 13, 2024, Eubanks signed a 2-year $10 million deal with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Sign Drew Eubanks|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-drew-eubanks|website=NBA.com|date=August 13, 2024|access-date=September 1, 2024}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2025)===
On February 1, 2025, (his 28th birthday), Eubanks was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] alongside [[Patty Mills]] in exchange for [[Mo Bamba]], [[P. J. Tucker]], a 2030 second-round pick and cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web|title=Clippers Acquire Eubanks and Mills from Utah|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-acquire-eubanks-and-mills-from-utah|website=NBA.com|date=February 1, 2025|access-date=February 1, 2025}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2025–2026)===
On July 8, 2025, the [[Sacramento Kings]] announced that they had signed Eubanks.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kings Sign Drew Eubanks|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-drew-eubanks|date=July 8, 2025|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 8, 2025}}</ref> He made 42 appearances (including 11 starts) for Sacramento during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 5.2 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 0.5 assists. On March 15, 2026, it was announced that Eubanks would require season-ending surgery to repair a torn [[ulnar collateral ligament of thumb|UCL]] in his left thumb.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kings center Drew Eubanks to undergo surgery on torn UCL in left thumb|url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/sacramento-kings/drew-eubanks-surgery-thumb-injury/1924223/?amp=1|access-date=May 10, 2026|website=nbcsportsbayarea.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Eubanks married his wife Hailey on August 20, 2022.<ref>{{cite web |website=www.wfaa.com |url=https://www.wfaa.com/article/sports/nba/spurs/spurs-celebrate-former-teammate-drew-eubanks-wedding-nba-san-antonio/273-65eae3cc-84e3-42e8-a5e0-92f5a482165c |title=Spurs celebrate former teammate Drew Eubanks' wedding |first=Jeff |last=Garcia |date=22 August 2022 |access-date=12 September 2022}}</ref>
His parents are David and Laura Eubanks.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://playerswiki.com/drew-eubanks#:~:text=Drew%20Eubanks%20Bio%20and%20Early%20Life%20Drew%20Eubanks,Eubanks%20and%20his%20mother%27s%20name%20is%20Laura%20Eubanks. |access-date=30 June 2024|title= Drew Eubanks }}</ref>
